Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

the final section should tell staff what still needs checking before the public version is sent to the print team include the tablet test the spelling review the link check the contact information decision and the room visit details please keep open tasks distinct from completed checks and leave space beside each task for a date and initials the final section needs to stay in the staff copy and should not appear on the public page also if the print copy is already prepared do not send another copy until the print team confirms which version they have received", "output": "I need help setting up a preview for the North Quay Archive before the Neighborhood History Weekend. The preview is not the full archive, and it should feel like a careful invitation to look around rather than a finished exhibition. We are opening the reading room on October 12, and the public preview should be ready for the staff walk-through on October 8. Please keep those dates separate because the print team needs the preview pages before the room is open, and the public will not see the reading room until the weekend.

For the first version, use material from the Harbor Collection only. There are 42 folders in that collection, and I want to show 12 folders in the preview, not all 42. Please make clear that 12 is the number selected for the preview and 42 is the full collection count. The selected folders should cover the ferry strike, the old fish market, and the winter storms, but please do not imply that those are the only subjects in the archive. Two folders should come from each of those three subjects, and the remaining six should show different kinds of material, including a ticket book, a hand-drawn map, and a set of letters.

For each preview item, include the folder title, the approximate date, the creator if we know it, a short description, and a note about any handling limits. Use an approximate date rather than a made-up exact day when the folder only has a month or a year. If the creator is not known, say “creator not identified.” Do not leave the field empty. Mark uncertain dates as uncertain, and keep that uncertainty in the description too. The item cards should be readable on a tablet without scrolling for a long time, so aim for about 70 words each. Please put the title first, not the archive reference number.

I also need a simple way for visitors to decide whether to turn on the small labels beside the photographs. Please use the configuration key below to control that option and leave the key exactly as written on its own line in the setup notes.
preview.show_labels
When the setting is on, show the short labels beside the photographs, and when it is off, keep the photographs visible but do not show those labels. Do not use this option to hide captions on the item cards; those captions are a separate part of the preview. The archive assistant said, “The labels should be helpful, not crowded,” so keep each one to one short sentence, and do not put a person’s full address on a label.

Please make the page work in this order: first, a short welcome that says what the preview covers; then a contents list; then the 12 item cards; then a note about visiting the reading room. The contents list should name each subject and show how many selected folders are in that subject. The count in the contents list needs to add up to 12. Include the approximate dates there if they help people choose, but do not let the dates take the place of the subject names. Use the title “Harbor Archive Preview” at the top, and include a small line saying “Prepared by the North Quay Archive Team.”

For the setup checklist: number one, check that every selected folder has a scan that opens on the staff tablet; number two, check the item card against the folder itself; and number three, check that the photograph labels follow the setting on the test page. Please use eight staff tablets for the walk-through. The change is eight tablets because two volunteers are joining the test, and we need one device for the front desk as well. The tablets are for staff testing and are not a count of devices for public visitors.

There is one condition that should affect the later review: if a folder contains a living person’s contact information, then do not put that scan in the public preview unless the archive manager has confirmed that the information can be shown. If confirmation has not arrived by October 7, leave that scan out of the preview and keep its folder title in the staff checklist so we can see that it was considered. This condition applies to scans and not to a general description of the folder. If a description itself gives contact details, shorten that description before it goes to the print team.

The print team needs a paper copy on October 6, and the digital version should be checked on October 7. Those are two different checks. Please ask Mara to look at spelling and ask Dev to check that the links open. Do not say they have approved the preview because they have not reviewed it yet. The archive manager will check the contact information condition, and the reading room coordinator will confirm the visit details after the staff walk-through. If any person cannot finish their part on the planned day, leave that check marked pending rather than guessing that it has happened.

For the public visit note, say that the reading room is on the ground floor of the North Annex and that visitors can ask the front desk for help. The room has a step-free entrance, but the two research tables are close together, so people using a wheelchair should contact the coordinator before arriving if they want a table held. Please keep that as an invitation, not a requirement, and do not promise a particular table. The weekend hours are 10 in the morning until 4 in the afternoon both days. The building closes at 4, so do not suggest that visitors can stay later.

We have also borrowed a listening station with three headphones, and it will play two short recordings from the ferry strike collection. Please say that the recordings are excerpts and that transcripts are available at the front desk. Do not describe them as complete interviews because one recording ends before the speaker finishes a sentence. If the listening station is unavailable, the item cards should still make sense without it, and the welcome should not tell people that listening is required.

Please use plain language, but keep the proper collection names and the exact folder titles from the catalog where they are provided. Put the catalog reference number in the staff checklist rather than in the visitor-facing title. Do not silently correct a title that looks unusual; ask me about it in a note for the staff version. If there is a mismatch between a scan and its catalog description, pause that item for review instead of choosing which one is right. I want the preview to be useful even if one item has to wait, and I do not want the remaining cards renumbered in a way that changes their catalog references.

The final section should tell staff what still needs checking before the public version is sent to the print team. Include the tablet test, the spelling review, the link check, the contact information decision, and the room visit details. Please keep open tasks distinct from completed checks and leave space beside each task for a date and initials. The final section needs to stay in the staff copy and should not appear on the public page. Also, if the print copy is already prepared, do not send another copy until the print team confirms which version they have received."}]
